questions.title: What Should You Do With Your Ball When There's a Thunderstorm?
questions.question: If you hear the horn or siren to stop play because of a thunderstorm, what should you do with your ball?

choices.text: Leave your ball where it is and go back to the clubhouse
Pick up your ball and leave, but don’t mark the spot
Put a marker by your ball, pick it up, and put it back later when you come back
Hurry up and hit your shot before leaving

questions.explanation: You need to put a marker by your ball, pick it up, and later place it back on the same spot when you come back to play.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Something small, like a coin or a special marker, that you put next to your ball to show where it was.
When everyone has to stop playing golf, often because of bad weather like a thunderstorm.

questions.teachingTip: Show children how to use a marker and practise picking up and putting back a ball in the same spot.
likelyMisconceptions: Some children may think they can just pick up the ball without marking where it was.
Some may want to quickly hit the ball before leaving.
Some might think they can just leave the ball on the ground.

questions.title: What to Do When Play Is Suspended Due to a Thunderstorm
questions.question: What must you do with your ball if play is stopped because of a thunderstorm warning signal?

choices.text: Leave it where it is and return to the clubhouse
Pick it up and take it with you without marking
Mark its position, lift it, and replace it later
Play your shot quickly before leaving

questions.explanation: You must mark where your ball lies, lift it, and later return it to exactly the same spot when play resumes.
